content: Initially, I was thinking if BitVec could be used for programming purposes as a compressed form of Array Bool but as I am reading the source code, it is not really suitable, right? For example getting a single bit looks like linear time operation (BitVec.getLsbD defined through Nat.testBit performs a shift of the full bitvector). Is my understanding correct?

Yeah I think there are two main problems:

  1. There are no constant time bit accessor functions (as you said)
  2. There are no functions that can modify a Nat in place

These together make working with Nat / BitVec as a bit set linear time.
Ok, so to have an efficient bitvector, one would have to implement it as Array UInt64, and build their own API for it.
Probably more like ByteArray because an Array UInt64 is an array of pointers to 16 byte allocations.
I see, I overestimated Lean's optimization capabilities.

Mirek Olšák said:

I see, I overestimated Lean's optimization capabilities.

This is not about Lean's optimization capabilities. Adding a constant time test bit function is entirely possible from within core its just not been done.
I meant the thing with Array UInt64 -- that I thought when it knows that UInt64 is unboxed, then it could put them in a raw form in the array.
But back to the original question, do you expect that efficient bitwise operations (mpz_setbit, mpz_clrbit, mpz_tstbit) will be eventually added to Nat?
I think that's entirely within the realm of possibilities
By the way, the original reason I asked this was different but now I needed it in my vibe-coding experiment, so here is an AI attempt of implementing efficient bit-operations on Nat: Lean, C++.
I recall @Sebastian Ullrich already did this on some branch for shake. Maybe we should merge it after all?
Note that not all Lean builds use GMP, so you'd need to add the API to Lean's internal mpz library too
(though it could be a non-optimal implementation)
Could you for start condition the @extern with availability of GMP?
I don't think writing the native implementation for Lean's internal mpz type would be much work
